info.name: OAuth — client_credentials
info.description:
The shortest end-to-end path through this provider: register a confidential client, then trade its secret for an access token (RFC 6749 §4.4).

Run the two requests in order. The first one writes `clientId` and `clientSecret` into the collection variables, so the second needs nothing typed in.

Before starting, set the `adminKey` variable to `ADMIN_API_KEY` from `auth-server/.env`. It is left empty here on purpose — this file is in version control and the key is not.

There is no refresh token in this flow: the token stands for the client itself, so when it expires the client asks again with its secret.

variable.description: ADMIN_API_KEY from auth-server/.env. Never commit it here.

exec: // The only time the plaintext secret is ever returned.

request.description:
Admin-only. `isPublic: false` is what gives the client a secret; a public one gets an empty string and could not authenticate here.

`grantTypes` is restricted to `client_credentials`, so this client cannot start an authorization code flow even if it tried.

exec: // §4.4.3: no refresh token here. The client re-authenticates instead.

request.description:
The credentials travel as HTTP Basic (RFC 7617), which is what `BasicTokenGuard` decodes.

`scope` is optional: drop it to receive everything the client is allowed, or narrow it to a subset. Asking for anything outside `allowedScopes` fails with `invalid_scope`.
